title: Burden of disease
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:38Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point describes Australia's health status through life expectancy and chronic disease, but it does not teach the burden of disease measure or DALYs, so it is a related idea rather than the same one.

draft.title: Burden of disease
card: Burden of disease measures the total impact of illness, injury and early death on a population. It counts both lives cut short and years lived in poor health.
The unit of measurement is the DALY, or disability-adjusted life year. One DALY is one year of healthy life lost.
A higher DALY total means a greater burden. Health planners can use DALYs to compare conditions and see where the most healthy life is being lost.
A condition can have a large burden because it kills many people, because it causes long illness or disability, or both.
draft.remember: Burden of disease is counted in DALYs: one DALY is one year of healthy life lost.

opts: One year of healthy life lost
One year spent in hospital care
One person who has a disability
a.why: A DALY is a unit of time: one year of healthy life lost to illness, injury or early death. It is not a count of people or deaths, which is the tempting mistake.
a.clue: Think of the unit as a length of time, not a head count.

b.q: A health agency finds that condition X caused 40,000 DALYs in a state last year and condition Y caused 25,000 DALYs. What can the agency conclude?
opts: X caused a greater burden of disease than Y
X killed more people than Y did
Y affects fewer people than X does
Y is less serious for each person than X
b.why: More DALYs means more healthy life lost, so X has the greater burden. DALYs do not show how many people died or how many were affected. A burden can come from long illness as well as deaths.
b.clue: DALYs add up healthy years lost, not people.

a.best: One year of healthy life lost

b.best: X caused a greater burden of disease than Y
